'''''Plagiochila''''' is a large, common, and widespread [[genus]] of [[liverwort]]s in the [[Order (biology)|order]] [[Jungermanniales]].<ref name="Schuster IV">{{cite book | last = Schuster | first = Rudolf M. | year = 1980 | title = The Hepaticae and Anthocerotae of North America | volume=IV | pages=342–539 | location=New York | publisher = Columbia University Press | isbn = 0-231-04608-1 }}</ref> It is a member of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]]  [[Plagiochilaceae]] within that order. There may be anywhere from 500 to 1,300 species, most of them from the tropics; the exact number is still under revision.  

== Biogeography ==
The genus has a cosmopolitan distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plagiochila (Dumort.) Dumort. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/2688968 |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=www.gbif.org |language=en}}</ref> 

There are nine species of ''Plagiochila'' in Britain and Ireland, the majority of which have a hyper-oceanic biogeography, demanding high humidity afforded by proximity to the Atlantic.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plagiochila spinulosa |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/plagiochila-spinulosa/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=British Bryological Society |language=en-GB}}</ref> The most widespread representative of the hyper-oceanic species is '''''Plagiochila spinulosa''''', a common species of Atlantic woodlands known as [[temperate rainforest]]. There is a disjunct population of ''Plagiochila spinulosa'' in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Renner |first1=Matt A. M. |last2=Heslewood |first2=Margaret M. |last3=Patzak |first3=Simon D. F. |last4=Feldberg |first4=Kathrin |last5=Schäfer-Verwimp |first5=Alfons |last6=Rycroft |first6=David S. |last7=Heinrichs |first7=Jochen |title=The New Zealand endemic ''Plagiochila caducifolia'' is a disjunct population of ''Plagiochila spinulosa'' (Plagiochilaceae: Jungermanniopsida) |journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany |date=2017-07-03 |volume=55 |issue=3 |pages=276–292 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0028825X.2017.1318756 |doi=10.1080/0028825x.2017.1318756 |bibcode=2017NZJB...55..276R |issn=0028-825X|url-access= }}</ref> 

== Taxonomy ==
''Plagiochila'' taxonomy is complex and disputed. Certain phylogenetic studies have shown that genetic distinctions between observed species are weak, suggesting recent diversification events.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Heinrichs |first1=J. |last2=Lindner |first2=M. |last3=Groth |first3=H. |last4=Renker |first4=C. |date=2005-01-01 |title=Distribution and synonymy of Plagiochila punctata (Taylor) Taylor, with hypotheses on the evolutionary history of Plagiochila sect. Arrectae (Plagiochilaceae, Hepaticae) |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00606-004-0220-5 |journal=Plant Systematics and Evolution |language=en |volume=250 |issue=1 |pages=105–117 |doi=10.1007/s00606-004-0220-5 |bibcode=2005PSyEv.250..105H |issn=1615-6110|url-access=subscription }}</ref> European species have been identified as conspecific or at least closely related to tropical American species, distinct from Asian species.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Groth |first1=Henk |last2=Lindner |first2=Melanie |last3=Wilson |first3=Rosemary |last4=Hartmann |first4=Florian A. |last5=Schmull |first5=Michaela |last6=Rob Gradstein |first6=S. |last7=Heinrichs |first7=Jochen |date=2003 |title=Biogeography of Plagiochila (Hepaticae): natural species groups span several floristic kingdoms |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1046/j.1365-2699.2003.00916.x |journal=Journal of Biogeography |language=en |volume=30 |issue=7 |pages=965–978 |doi=10.1046/j.1365-2699.2003.00916.x |bibcode=2003JBiog..30..965G |issn=1365-2699|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
